newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-MARTIN BUILDS THREE-STROKE LEAD IN CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MARTIN BUILDS THREE-STROKE LEAD IN CLASSIC.

text.p: Spain's Miguel Angel Martin shrugged off an Australian summer heatwave on Saturday to build up a three-stroke lead heading into the final round of the Heineken Classic.
On a day on which temperatures reached 44 degrees Celsius, Martin fired a bogey-free round, his third for the tournament, of 65 to boast a three-round total of 202, 14 under par
Consistent New Zealander Frank Nobilo eagled the 473-metre par five 18th to card a 70 and finish on 11 under par.
A further stroke back were Ireland's Paul McGinley and Padraig Harrington, Briton Paul Eales, Australia's Wayne Riley and Japan's Katsuyoshi Tomori.

Riley, fresh from a 66 on Friday, steadily climbed up the leaderboard and was in a tie for the lead at 11-under with Harrington after making his fourth birdie for the day on the par five 493-metre 10th.
But Riley lost his direction on the 391-metre par four 11th, ending up with a triple-bogey seven. He was able to make amends on the 18th by knocking in a three-metre eagle putt.
Lurking on nine-under and within striking distance were American Fred Couples, French pair Jean Van De Velde and Marc Farry and Australian Rodney Pampling.
Britain's Ian Woosnam was on six under par after carding a third-round 69.
But Martin could prove hard to catch after 54 solid holes.
"I'm playing great at the moment, fantastic," Martin said.
"It's the best I've played ever -- I have only missed three greens and have had no bogeys in three days."
Martin, whose only victory on the European Tour was in the French Open in 1992, said he was not concerned by the heat.
"I didn't feel it was too hot and back home in Madrid in summer we play in 44 and 45 degrees."
South African Ernie Els turned in 33 and then picked up another stroke coming in to finish with a solid 68 and be four under for the tournament.

Els' playing partner for the first two days, John Daly, had a nightmare round, racking up triple and double bogeys and six bogeys to finish with an 83. The American was trailing the field at 10 over par.
